newsitem.title: YUGOSLAVIA: Yugo Komercijalna bank to get DM10 mln credit line.
newsitem.headline: Yugo Komercijalna bank to get DM10 mln credit line.

text.p: Berliner Bank of Germany has agreed to open a 10 million German mark credit line to Komercijalna Banka a.d. for supporting trade between the two countries, the Belgrade media reported on Wednesday.
The credit arrangement was signed during a two-day visit of a 60-member delegation of German bankers and businessmen to Belgrade.
Komercijalna Banka vice-president Panta Plazinic said details would be available early next week. Komercijalna Banka, a leading Yugoslav private bank, emerged from the leading state bank Jugobanka.
"Berliner Bank board of directors is yet to decide on all terms such as maturity, interest rates and whether it (the credit line) will be used to finance imports or exports," Plazinic told Reuters.
But Borka Vucic, a leading Yugoslav banker, said she was disappointed by the overall performance of the German bankers.

"We felt a strong will among German partners to enter new deals even before the International Monetary Fund recognizes continuity to Yugoslavia, but not among German banks. They are waiting for a go-ahead by their government," Vucic was quoted as saying by daily newspaper Novosti.
According to Vucic, Germany and its banks seem to lag other countries in clinching deals with Yugoslav companies.
The German deputy economy minister Hans Schill warned Yugoslavia was now competing for German investments against many countries including those from Asia.

"There is readiness on our part but much has to be done on the part of Yugoslavia regarding reforms and overall liberalisation of the economy," Schill told a gathering of Yugoslav and German businessmen.

He insisted Yugoslavia had to do more on privatisation, restructuring of the banking sector and other reforms in order to bring the economic systems of the countries closer. -- Gordana Filipovic, Belgrade newsroom, +381 11 222 4254
